sourceObjectiveEnglish: Refer back without repeating: Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with it: el libro → lo; las llaves → las.
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Un libro prestado with a patient classmate. Practice refer back without repeating. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

sourceGrammarEnglish.focus: Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with it: el libro → lo; las llaves → las. Put the pronoun before a conjugated verb.

examples.es: Ella lo tiene en su mochila.
examples.en: She has it in her backpack.

cards.decisionNote: Spanish me covers object and reflexive uses. French me/moi varies by syntax; choose contextual examples rather than one answer.
Source mochila is feminine; French sac à dos is masculine. Its object pronoun is le/l', not la.
Source clase groups class session and classroom. The Reader's después de clase means after class; cours is contextual.
Source el is masculine singular. French le elides to l' before a vowel and requires a noun context.
Source la groups feminine article, object it and person her. French la/l' and lui differ by grammatical role.
Source un is masculine singular; French un must agree with the chosen noun.
Source en covers in/on/at; French dans, sur, à and au depend on the phrase.
Spanish tengo is I have; French j'ai is a contextual conjugation, while source pronoun placement needs separate teaching.
Spanish necesito is I need; French avoir besoin de changes the construction and contracts in du/des.
Source los is masculine plural article or object pronoun. French les does not encode that masculine contrast.

cards.proposedFrench: J'ai besoin du livre de Julia.

cards.sourceSpanish: Ella lo tiene en su mochila.
cards.sourceEnglish: She has it in her backpack.
cards.proposedFrench: Elle l'a dans son sac à dos.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish lo refers to masculine libro; French l' elides le before a and son agrees with masculine sac à dos.

cards.sourceSpanish: Le pido el libro después de clase.
cards.sourceEnglish: I ask her for the book after class.
cards.proposedFrench: Je lui demande le livre après le cours.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish le is an indirect object for Julia; French lui, unlike la, marks the recipient. Après le cours keeps the class-session sense.

cards.sourceSpanish: Julia me lo presta por un día.
cards.sourceEnglish: Julia lends it to me for one day.
cards.proposedFrench: Julia me le prête pour une journée.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish me lo and French me le preserve indirect recipient plus direct object order; por un día is duration, not purpose.

cards.sourceEnglish: I read it in the library.
cards.proposedFrench: Je le lis à la bibliothèque.

cards.sourceEnglish: Afterward I return the book to her.
cards.proposedFrench: Ensuite, je lui rends le livre.

cards.sourceSpanish: Busco el libro y lo encuentro.
cards.sourceEnglish: I look for the book and find it.
cards.proposedFrench: Je cherche le livre et je le trouve.

cards.sourceSpanish: Tengo la mochila y la abro.
cards.sourceEnglish: I have the backpack and open it.
cards.proposedFrench: J'ai le sac à dos et je l'ouvre.
cards.decisionNote: Source feminine mochila becomes masculine sac à dos; French l' is elided le here, not evidence that both nouns share gender.

reader.proposedFrench: J'ai besoin du livre de Julia.

reader.sourceSpanish: Ella lo tiene en su mochila.
reader.sourceEnglish: She has it in her backpack.
reader.proposedFrench: Elle l'a dans son sac à dos.
reader.decisionNote: French l' hides the book's masculine pronoun shape; show le livre → le → l' explicitly in grammar.

reader.sourceSpanish: Le pido el libro después de clase.
reader.sourceEnglish: I ask her for the book after class.
reader.proposedFrench: Je lui demande le livre après le cours.
reader.decisionNote: Keep indirect lui for Julia distinct from direct le for the book.

reader.sourceSpanish: Julia me lo presta por un día.
reader.sourceEnglish: Julia lends it to me for one day.
reader.proposedFrench: Julia me le prête pour une journée.
reader.decisionNote: French me le order is central to this lesson; validate the recipient and duration senses.

reader.sourceEnglish: I read it in the library.
reader.proposedFrench: Je le lis à la bibliothèque.

reader.sourceEnglish: Afterward I return the book to her.
reader.proposedFrench: Ensuite, je lui rends le livre.

reader.sourceSpanish: Busco el libro y lo encuentro.
reader.sourceEnglish: I look for the book and find it.
reader.proposedFrench: Je cherche le livre et je le trouve.

reader.sourceSpanish: Tengo la mochila y la abro.
reader.sourceEnglish: I have the backpack and open it.
reader.proposedFrench: J'ai le sac à dos et je l'ouvre.
reader.decisionNote: Spanish la marks feminine mochila, but French sac à dos requires le/l'. Keep the cross-language gender change visible.

reader.sourceSpanish: Compro los cuadernos y los guardo.
reader.sourceEnglish: I buy the notebooks and put them away.
reader.proposedFrench: J'achète les cahiers et je les range.
reader.decisionNote: French les for notebooks is plural without Spanish masculine agreement; this contrast needs explicit explanation.

reader.sourceSpanish: Necesito las llaves, pero no las veo.
reader.sourceEnglish: I need the keys, but I do not see them.
reader.proposedFrench: J'ai besoin des clés, mais je ne les vois pas.
reader.decisionNote: French les for keys is also plural without Spanish feminine agreement; include both noun contexts.

reader.sourceSpanish: Ana tiene el lápiz y lo usa.
reader.sourceEnglish: Ana has the pencil and uses it.
reader.proposedFrench: Ana a le crayon et elle l'utilise.
reader.decisionNote: French l' elides masculine le before utilise; preserve the pencil antecedent.
Spanish la is feminine, but its antecedent is not explicit in this isolated line. French l' also hides gender. Qualified source/curriculum review must select the referent before scoring.

archivedRedesign.title: Réparer une référence ambiguë
archivedRedesign.scene: Deux organisatrices et deux dossiers sont mentionnés. Un pronom ambigu provoque une confusion sur le destinataire et l’objet.
archivedRedesign.reason: The archived Nadia/Camille folder-handoff and ambiguous-recipient repair change the source borrowed-book scene and direct-object objective; they cannot inherit this lesson's saved positions or recordings.

sourceDecisions: Source lo/la/los/las agreement needs French le/la/les and elision taught with explicit book, backpack, notebook and key antecedents. French les does not retain source plural gender.
Source direct-object objective also includes indirect le and me lo in the Reader; choose a clear progression for le/la/les versus lui and me le rather than silently changing the source objective.
Source final ¿La tienes tú? lacks an explicit antecedent in that line. Decide the intended feminine object before assigning a French answer or saved-item mapping.
Source class/classroom, mochila/sac à dos, in/on/at, and article/object-pronoun headwords need contextual dictionary senses; French grammatical gender and elision must be explicit.
The source places beginner direct-object pronouns at Master 17; qualified curriculum review must decide progression while preserving the stage-local progress identity.
